bio: Another LMDh / GTP car on the service, the Acura ARX-06 is one of Acura's racing thoroughbreds designed and built to take on BMW, Cadillac, Ferrari, and Porsche. The car features many innovations, technology, and impressive performance figures guaranteed to make it one to watch out for on raceday. To start off, the car has a carbon fiber monocoque chassis and a double wishbone with pushrod suspension front and rear with Penske dampers giving the car ample durability, toughness, and a comfortable handling model that will be well-suited for many drivers alike. Other features on the car include a FIA-specified roll cage structure, carbon fiber driver's seat shell, six-point safety harness, fresh air intake system, and on-board fire suppression system for max safety for the driver. With an IMSA-specified XTrac six-speed, sequential, paddle-operated transmission and a engine producing over 650 hp, this makes the Acura ARX-06 a LMDh / GTP car ready for the battlegrounds of raceday war.

Another GT3 addition to a very healthy field, Acura's NSX GT3 Evo 22 storms onto the racing scene to compete against Audi, BMW, Chevrolet, Ferrari, Ford, Lamborghini, McLaren, Mercedes-Benz, and Porsche. Featuring a powerful 3.5L Twin-Turbocharged DOHC V6 ICE engine making just over 500 horsepower, while it has less power than a number of its counterparts, it seems adequate for its weight, fuel mileage, and acceleration time. The car also features the latest in GT3 racing technology like an aluminum monocoque with a steel roof structure, a short-long arm double wishbone and multilink with outboard coilover spring suspension, Brembo piston with steel rotors and ABS braking, and a 6 speed sequential transmission makes the car worthy of an opponent for its hardened veteran adversaries.

The newest ARCA Chevrolet vehicle to hit the iRacing scene, the ARCA Chevrolet SS is definitely a high speed oval racer for many racing tracks from tight short ovals to the big superspeedways. The car features General racing tires, a Holley 4150HP Series carburetor, Five star composite laminate blend body, a steel tubeframe chassis, and the usual 4 speed manual transmission with no clutch needed to shift to the higher gears from 2 to 4. With a beefy 700 horsepower coming from its ARCA Ilmor 396 cubic inch V8 engine, the car is loud and proud to thrill ARCA fans alike for many racedays to come.

Featuring the same features as its Chevrolet and Toyota rivals, the ARCA Ford Mustang is a nice alternative to those that are neither Chevrolet or Toyota fans. Between the exterior look of the cars, there isn't a whole lot in terms of differences. With that the car features the same General racing tires, a Holley 4150HP Series carburetor, Five star composite laminate blend body, a steel tubeframe chassis, and the usual 4 speed manual transmission including the ARCA Ilmore 396 Cubic Inch V8 engine giving this pony express a lot of muscle needed to race against its most fiercest competitors.

With speeds topping out at almost 205 mph and 650 horsepower under the hood, this Impala is ready for action out on the track. The older Gen 4 variant of this classic NASCAR design is still used today in the ARCA Meanrds Series. Its Chevy Pushrod 358 Cubic Inch V8 makes it one of the most powerful Oval Racecars to date. Though the weight is at around 3300 lbs and acceleration to 60 mph in just under 4 seconds, the drivers, fans, and sponsors can truly agree that this vehicle is one of the best oval racers in the world. Many people flock to the races that these cars visit to see what kind of action, fun, and entertainment has in store waiting for them.

With different exterior looks compared to its Ford or Chevrolet ARCA car rivals, the ARCA Toyota Camry is still a fine choice for anyone picking an ARCA vehicle for raceday. Once again, the car has the same features as the other two options with the same General racing tires, a Holley 4150HP Series carburetor, Five star composite laminate blend body, a steel tubeframe chassis, and the usual 4 speed manual transmission including the ARCA Ilmore 396 Cubic Inch V8 engine makes the ARCA Toyota Camry one of the most modern oval racing vehicles in America today.

engine: V12 DOHC with 4 valves per cylinder
bio: Speed and Power are matched in the form of the DBR9 GT1. The car is designed for Le Mans series racing and a tough breed to beat. The V12 DOHC engine produces over 600 horsepower giving the car weight under 3000 lbs and fast acceleration at the 3 second mark. The aluminium frame with carbon fibre panels lowers the cars weight while its double wishbone with adjustable Koni dampers give the car a more flexible feel. With Eibach springs for its suspension, it shows other racing cars in the GT1 category that this Brit Car is worth staying around.

The Aston Martin Valkyrie AMR-LMH is the 4th and newest Aston Martin car to join iRacing. The addition of this car also marks the 17th vehicle from the United Kingdom and now the nation has a high speed LMDh vehicle to call its own. The car is powered by a 6.5 Liter Naturally Aspirated V12 engine making 671 horsepower propelling it easily past 200 mph. The other features of the car include a Xtrac 7 speed transmission, a Multimatic Carbon Tub chassis, a double wishbone suspension, 6 pot Alcon caliper brakes, and Michelin tires giving the car a very modern and technologically advanced feel like no other.

iRacing's newest Aston Martin on the service since the Vantage GT4, the Vantage GT3 EVO features the usual refinements that GT3 drivers have expected over the years. The car is powered by 4.0L DOHC V8 ICE Twin-Turbocharged engine delivering over 530 horsepower and a 6 speed sequential transmission. Other refinements of the car include a large 28 gallon or 106 liter fuel tank, an aluminum monocoque chassis with bonded and bolted steel safety cage, a short-long arm double wishbone with outboard coilover springs and dampers on the suspension, and Alcon brakes with 6-piston action on the front and 4-piston action in the rear with steel rotors and ABS making this Aston Martin one of the most advanced GT3 cars competing today.

More GT4 cars for the diehard GT4 fans, the Aston Martin Vantage does that and deliver. With a 450 hp 4.7L V8 engine under the hood the car packs the punch as it cruises effortlessly up to 170 mph. The car itself has a 27.8 gallon fuel tank for long range endurance racing and a 3200+ lb total weight for maximum punishment out on the racetrack. The gearbox is a 6-speed manual sequential with flappy paddles connected to a mechanical self-locking differential while also having front and rear indepenent coilover suspension and Ohlins own ILX 2-way adjustable dampers giving the car the agility and handling it needs. With over 425 ft lbs of torque, this car has the muscle to take it to Porsche, BMW, and Audi for any GT4 race.

The Audi 90 GTO is one of the classic IMSA cars of its time that showcased power, speed, and handling to the track. It’s Inline Five Cylinder engine is no slouch and drivers know it. The Inline Five Cylinder Turbocharged engine is well known for being the Audi Quattro S1 Pikes Peak power of choice. Its 6 speed gearbox makes acceleration a breeze to go through. It's standard steel roof and tubular frame isn't very technologically advanced but for the late 1980's, its one hyper performance of a racing car that should never be overlooked.

engine: Audi 4.0 Liter V6 turobdiesel and Electric motor-generator
bio: A LMP1 Rival to Porsche, this Audi R18 is throwing all its power onto the pavement to show who’s #1 at Le Mans. This car is truly a screamer. The car features a Double a-arm suspension at both ends and the front uses a pushrod-actuated heave element, anti-roll bar, and roll damper. The rear suspension uses a pullrod-actuated heave element, anti-roll bar, torsion bars, and roll damper. The six-speed paddle actuated, semi-automatic transmission allows no mis-shifts at all and allows upshifts and downshifts a breeze.The carbon discs with monobloc calipers and an electronic control for brake balance uses a re-generating hybrid system to keep the car balanced and smooth on the race track. With a powerful diesel engine for the rear wheels and an electric motor generator for the front wheels, this car and its 17.6 gallon fuel tank proves to be quite the brute force of a racecar Audi set out to create.

engine: 90 degree V10, DOHC, 4 valves per cylinder
bio: When power comes to shove, the Audi R8 LMS can get the job done for GT and Sports Cars alike. Its DOHC V10 engine gives it vast power while keeping the tires to the asphalt. The Electro hydraulically activated 3-plate race clutch and its double wishbone with coil springs and adjustable dampers give this car unmatched tech like no other. Based on the designs and looks of the first Audi R8 Le Mans Quattro of 2006 and later 2010, it has transferred to this magnificent car for racing enthusiasts to enjoy.

wiki_title: Audi R8 LMS EVO II GT3
bio: One of Audi's newest GT3 racers comes to iRacing in the form of the R8 LMS EVO II. The car is a 585 horsepower fire-breathing dragon that gives its naturally aspirated 5.2L V10 engine the punch it deserves. The car also has over 550 nm of torque for bursting acceleration and even features a sequential, pneumatically six-speed performance transmission for optimal gear shifting. With a new aerodynamics package that generates more downforce on the rear wing, a new intake system, and four-way adjustable dampers in the suspension, the car itself has the performance and technology to deal even with the most fiercest GT3 competitors out on the track.

The new Audi RS3 LMS Gen2 TCR seems to be the TCR answer out on the circuit. The car may have 10 less horsepower compared to its previous generation but it still remains a fierce competitor on any track in any touring car series. A 6 speed sequential transmission combined with a Audi RS3 motorsports adapted body shell with a full carbon fiber bodywork for its chassis gives it great flexibility and acceleration for its 4 cylinder 2.0 liter turbocharged engine. Other features include a strut front multilink rear suspension, Alon 6 piston front caliper and 2 piston rear brakes and Michelin tires gives the car all the usual touring car refinements and technology that's expected but improved upon compared to its previous generation.

One of the newest brutes to iRacing, the Audi RS3 LMS TCR is ready to tear up the racetrack for spectacular fun. A very sturdy vehicle makes it a truly reliable spectacle for all race fans. The car features McPherson suspension for easy adjustability on the toe, camber, and even the height with multi-link accessibility. A VAQ electro-hydraulic and its 3 modes keep the differential nice and smooth through the cars weight distribution giving it an even keel. With 6-piston caliper brakes for maximum stopping power, this Audi RS3 LMS TCR is ready for any brutal TCR race come shine, night, cloudy, or even rainy weather.

wiki_title: BMW M Hybrid V8 EVO LMDh / GTP
engine: V-shaped P66/3 Otto four-stroke twin-turbocharged V8
bio: The first LMDh car to hit the iRacing racing scene, the BMW M Hybrid V8 EVO LMDh / GTP is truly a remarkable racecar in both performance, technology, and economy. Starting off, the car features a V-shaped P66/3 Otto four-stroke twin-turbocharged V8 with a Front-mounted separate motor generator single-speed reducer for a juicy 640 horses of power. The car has cast aluminum cylinder block and cylinder head construction for durability and strength to keep the car intact at all times. The car also has high-pressure direct injection at 350 bar for mean effective pressure and a dry sump oil system for superb lubrication and with a 7 speed transmission gives this car plenty of acceleration during any race event to leave its competition in the dust.

Something a bit different, the BMW M2 CS Racing (F87) - 2020 is quite a different car altogether for the base content side of iRacing. Mainly being used as a gap between rookie content and the GT4 and TCR cars, the car features a 3.0 Liter Inline 6-Cylinder, 4 valve engine capable of making around 365 horsepower with a 7 Speed BMW DSG transmission. The car has a steel body with aluminum and carbon for its chassis, a strut and multilink system for its suspension, Alcon piston brakes, and Michelin Pilot Sport GT tires giving the car a balanced feel between its handling, braking, and the power that it delivers to the track. With the car being an entry-level racer, this vehicle is sure to be quite a fan favorite.

The newest update from Bavaria, the BMW M2 CS Racing (G87) is a landmark upgrade from the previous F87 model. One of BMW's latest cars for road racing, the new G87 features racecar technology that makes it popular among many drivers and fans alike. Some new technological advancements include a 7 Speed ZF Automatic Gearbox, a Turbocharged 2.0 L B48B20O1 Inline 4 engine, a Steel unibody chassis, MacPherson strut front and multi-link rear suspension, BMW 6 piston front, 1 piston rear with iron rotor brakes, and Goodyear tires that gives the car the grip and handling that it desires making this new G87 model quite a technologically advanced car indeed.

The M4 F82 GT4 is BMW’s latest design in power and maximum aerodynamics in the GT4 field. With competing makers from Porsche, McLaren, Audi, and others, BMW has definitely got a car with a lot of punch. The car features a Twin-Turbo 3.0-Liter Inline-Six engine for max horsepower output of 431 horses. A 33.6 gallon fuel tank for maximum endurance, weight of over 3100 lbs to stick the car to the road, and also a 0-60 mph time of 3.7 seconds makes the BMW M4 GT4 quite a spectacle of a racecar,

engine: 3.0 Liter ICE Turbo Charged Inline 6 Cylinder
bio: The newest GT4 on the block, the BMW M4 G82 GT4 Evo is ready to hit the racing scene taking on the Porsche, Aston Martin, McLaren, and Mercedes-Benz equivalents. Replacing the previous F82 model, this car comes packed with new racecar features and has over 500 hp thanks to its 3.0 Liter ICE Turbo Charged Inline 6 Cylinder engine. The car does weigh slightly heavier than its older F82 counterpart but no matter what, the acceleration has been slightly improved from a 3.7 second time to a new 3.3 second time. A slightly larger fuel tank to improve its range and a 7 speed semi-automatic transmission with stamped steel chassis and carbon fiber components and strut front multilink suspension AP Racing 6 piston caliper brakes makes this car a true technical GT4 car in a long line of innovation history.

BMW's newest EVO GT3 racer, the M4 EVO GT3 combines modern technology with cutting edge power and speed. The vehicle itself is powered by a Water-Cooled Turbocharged Inline 6 that makes just over 500 horsepower. One of the many features on the car include the ever popular Brembo racing calipers for max stopping and braking power. Its suspension is double A-arms with coilovers on the front and rear with KW 4-way adjustable dampers and also blade-adjustable front and rear anti-roll bars for the best stability and handling on the circuit. The transmission is a 6-speed sequential transaxle gearbox with also a valvetrain that is a DOHC and a direct fuel injection fuel feed. With also dry sump lubrication and even a weight of just over 2800 lbs, this car is ready to go for any driver that knows how to get the most out of any GT3 machinery.

The new M8 GTE, is BMW’s answer to the GTE world. With over 500 horsepower at the disposal and top speeds over 180 mph, this new Beemer will take the fight to Ford, Porsche, Ferrari and more to secure dominance in an already crowded racing field. The car also features Brembo racing caliper brakes for maximum stopping during anytime a wreck occurs in front of it. The vehicle is also installed with Front and rear Double A-arms with coil over suspension with cartridge type dampers to ensure a safe ride over bumps on various racetracks. Michelin tires are supplied on the car to ensure maximum grip and traction whenever needed and finally, the 6-speed transaxle sequential gearbox ensures no misshifts are allowed whatsoever. This gives the car a more friendly appearance in both operation and usage out on the track.

Pure German engineering is displayed in the form of the Z4 GT3. BMW’s V8 engine gives it over 500 hp with unmatched handling ability. The car is one of BMW’s pride in the racing world. Based on the roadgoing BMW Z4, this GT3 version has been upgraded to include more sophistaced aero, winglets, and front fenders to provide even more additional downforce. The MacPherson axle with pushrods and wishbone give the car a ride quality like no other, tailored for its own racing driver. The H&R Coil Springs help the suspension while its two proprietary lubricants keep the car running until the race is over.

engine: 6.2L V8 with aluminum block and heads
bio: A 6.2L V8 and over 450 horsepower make the CTS-V Racecar a true GT style racer. Its top speed of almost 190 mph makes it a true racer when always driving on road courses all across the entire world. With a rear wing to provide more downforce for the back end of the car, it still remains a powerful beast today. While the racing modifications have improved its worth to the track, this CTS-V Racecar today has been blown away by newer, more tech-savvy cars of the future for safer but still more dynamic racing.

The newest LMDh/ GTP car to join the iRacing service, the new Cadillac V-Series.R is the main competitor to BMW's M Hybrid V8 LMDh/ GTP car making these 2 fierce beasts requiring new techniques and skills that are needed in order to tame them. The car comes with all the latest innovations and technology associated with LMDh / GTP cars and even some other features of its own. The car has a 7-Speed Sequential gearbox with a dry sump for its lubrication system and a Rear-mounted 50KW spec MGU for some extra boost for qualifying, overtake, build, no deploy, or attack modes, a feature also seen on a few other cars that are on the iRacing service. The Xtrac P1359 7-speed carbon-fibre plastics reinforced pneumatically actuated transmission makes the car a breeze to shift through the gears, both upshifting and downshifting, which gives the vehicle to struck a cord with even more iRacing service members.

engine: 2.0 Litre Ford Duratec Naturally Aspirated Inline 4
bio: The Caterham 420R is the other Caterham car that iRacing has brought to the service and boats 65 more horsepower compared to its less powerful Academy cousin with 195 hp compared to 130 hp. The car is powered by a 2.0 Litre Ford Duratec Naturally Aspirated Inline 4 engine and has a SADEV 6 speed sequential transmission. The car has similar features to its Academy alternate which includes a Tube frame with aluminum skin, a double wishbone and de-dion suspension, and 4 piston AP Racing calipers with iron discs. The car has Nova tires so the car is light and nimble on its wheels but still powerful enough to challenge a MX-5 and even a Formula Ford car for both speed and acceleration making it quite a formidable adversary as a racecar for climbing up the racing hierarchy.

The Caterham Academy car is iRacing's first entry for Caterham vehicles as the car comes in a double package with it and the 420R. The Academy car itself comes with its own set of features which includes a 6 Speed H-Pattern transmission, a Tube frame with aluminum skin Chassis, a Double wishbone front with de-dion rear axle suspension, Toyo Tires, and 2 piston AP racing sliding calipers on iron discs making this car a very modern Caterham vehicle for raceday, trackday, or even a simple day out on the road just to cruise about.

With a LSR7 6980cc V8 engine, the Corvette C6.R GT1 has a speed prepared for Le Mans style racing come rain, shine, or cloudy weather. Being based on its roadgoing counterpart, Pratt and Miller engineering designed and developed the car for high levels of intense racing around the globe. Featuring CNC Ported Cylinder heads, Titanium Valves with a Steel forged crankshaft, the car and its modifications gave the overall vehicle 6% less drag than the standard roadgoing vehicle.

A 5.5 Liter V8 gives the C7 Daytona Prototype the king of the Prototype racing out there. With its steel tube frame being made in consolidation with Dallara, the car and its double wishbone, push-rod actuated coil springs give it a smooth but firm ride around the race track. The sequential semi-automatic 6 speed transmission makes changing up and down gears a breeze to go through ensuring drivers to never allow a misshift or put in the wrong gear. Having 4 constructors championships and 3 drivers championships over its lifetime, its one of the most successful Daytona Prototype cars in the motorsport world of racing.

The latest Corvette GTE monster that has now been unveiled to the racing world, the Chevrolet Corvette C8.R GTE is the newest GTE competitor in the iRacing field. Now taking the fight to BMW, Porsche, Ferrari, and Ford this fire breathing American muscle car is ready to crush its competition. Using a naturally aspirated 5.5 liter V8 that produces 500 horsepower and revving up to 7200 rpm, the car also features a six speed sequential transmission to ensure the smoothest of any upshift or downshift. The car also has a very quick acceleration 0-60 mph (0-100 kmh) time of 3.2 seconds giving it a middle range between the Porsche's quick 2.9 seconds and BMW's semi-quick 3.5 seconds. With a weight of 2,733 pounds, the car is a true midweight and its competition surely knows it. Michelin tires give it the superb traction and grip it needs to blast through any corners which makes this car a worthy adversary.

engine: 5.5 Liter Naturally Aspirated Flat-Plane Crankshaft DOHC V8
bio: With the 2023 season behind them, Chevrolet looked forwards to a new beginning for the 2024 season with the Corvette Z06 GT3.R for its competition racecar. This vehicle itself, still under the Corvette Racing program, still carries the Corvette Racing traits that has been in circulation for decades. With a 5.5 Liter Naturally Aspirated Flat-Plane Crankshaft DOHC V8 engine and a Xtrac 6 speed gearbox, the car has the ample power and torque needed to power its way through straights and out of the bends on any racetrack even though its a bit heavier than some of its older cousins. Double Wishbone suspension and a fully homologated FIA safety cage and crash safety systems makes it a technological right-up-to-date thoroughbred with the addition of even Quick-fill Fuel Fill and AP Racing Calipers and even optimized driveline systems makes this car a true marvel in its own right.

With new technology, Dallara brings out their latest Formula racing monster, the F312 F3. This new car combines performance and economy to create a open wheeled racecar like no other. Being a beginner F1 car, it will be the envy of Renault’s Formula 3.5. The chassis is made from a carbon fiber monocoque giving strong rigidity and strengthness when taking in hits out on the track. It also features a Hewland 6-speed sequential transmission to minimize driver error when upshifting or downshifting. With a Naturally Aspirated Inline 4-Cylinder engine with 220 horsepower and weight of just over 1200 lbs, this car can really show some of the others what it can do.

A rocket car with acceleration and speed to boast, the IL-15 is a open wheel car that is sure to turn some heads from its 450 horsepower 2.0L Inline-4 Cylinder Turbocharged engine. The 6 speed sequential transmission coupled with a carbon fiber tub chassis thats also throughout its bodywork and both front and rear wings give it lightweight properties to give some cars a run for their money. Other features on this car include a double wishbone suspension on the front and rear with pushrods and a rocker activated inboard damper system with PFC style brakes with 6-piston action on the front and rear with iron rotors. With Firestone tires, this IL-15 can show what it can do not on just the straights but also in the turns too.

A new high speed monster for the road racing aficionados, the Dallara IR-01 encapsulates power, speed, handling, and much more like no any open wheel racecar ever before. The power from its 3.0 liter naturally aspirated V10 makes this car squeal loud and proud to the tune of F1 cars of the mid 2000's. With a high speed of 245 mph (394 kmh) and an acceleration time that only rivals that of the Nissan GTP ZX-T, this car is truly a monster. Drivers that want to master this vehicle have a lot of work ahead of them but it will surely pay off in the end when their victories come to fruition. While the car itself can go much faster, its final drive ratio disbands it from going any faster, likely for a number of safety reasons.

The newest Indycar entry offered, the Indycar IR18 is a vast improvement over its DW12 counterpart. With a slim design look and a smaller rear wing, this car was designed to cut through the air like a missile. This car is an untamed monster to any that drives it. The car features a Double A-arm, pushrod, with third spring and anti-roll bar on both the front and rear to create a perfect and balanced suspension. The sequential six speed, paddle actuated, semi-automatic transmission ensures that a misshift is impossible to perform no matter who is driving the car. With PFC carbon disc brakes with monobloc aluminum calipers, this car is ready to do many laps around the track without breaking a single sweat.

A fast new Dallara for the road racing experience, the Dallara P217 LMP2 is a perfect blend of LMP1 acceleration with GTE dependability. While not having much more power than their slower GTE counterparts, the new Dallara P217 LMP2 makes up for that with less weight, better aerodynamics, better downforce, and less drag to give it the straight line acceleration it deserves. Featuring a Gibson GK-428 4.2 liter V8 engine producing 608 horsepower and an acceleration 0-60 mph (0-100 kmh) time of 3.1 seconds, this car and its Michelin tires and Brembo carbon disc brakes make this car reliable, sturdy, fast, and fun for any road racer. The car also features double wishbone independent pushrod on its suspension and a chassis made entirely out of carbon-fibre with a monocoque design with aluminium honeycomb and zylon side panels that makes this car a technological dream. Finally, its Xtrac P1159F 6 speed sequential semi-automatic paddle-shift transmission makes the shifting very smooth, precise, and very effecient. This Dallara can stir up any competition that comes its way.

A true beginners Dirt Introduction car, the Dirt Legends Ford ‘34 Coupe gives drivers what it feels like to drive on the loose stuff. Skill is the key to master this car. As the dirt version of its Legends Ford '34 Coupe counterpart, this vehicle is the perfect entry for Dirt Ovals and to learn the basics on dirt track racing. Being part of the 600 Racing family, this dirt version of the Legends Ford '34 Coupe, drivers will enjoy the fun and thrill of this classic vehicle.

With its 350 Cubic Inch, 425 hp Chevrolet, the Dirt Street Stock is one different machine. Because of its high weight, it requires braking into the turns but trying not to hit the wall or spinning out. Built by the JR Motorsports group who also put together the rookie Street Stock vehicle, the small wing but high dirt car speeds it attains still remains a challenge to dirt track drivers today.

The new Euro NASCAR V8GP is the first outside of America racing series that gets big focus in the world of simracing. While most NASCAR cars on iRacing are mainly focused on modifieds, trucks, O'Reilly, or Cup series that is mainly centered in North America. the Euro NASCAR V8GP takes its focus abroad over on the continent of Europe. The car features a 5.7 Liter V8 Small Block engine, a 5 speed sequential transmission, a tube frame chassis, a front independent with live rear axle suspension, and 4 pot caliber brakes gives this car a modern technological feel without making it too old school.

engine: V6 120 degree turbo dry sump 2992 cc
bio: A new type of Ferrari racing, the 296 Challenge is definitely one of the most formidable road racing cars around the globe today. From the illustrious F355 Challenge to the impeccable F430 Challenge and more, the new 296 Challenge and the series it participates in today seems to be carrying that Ferrari Challenge torch bright. With that said, the new Ferrari 296 Challenge car features modern Ferrari refinements including a 7 speed F1 dual clutch transmission, Pirelli tires, front disc and rear disc brakes, and a V6 120 degree turbo dry sump 2992 cc engine making 700 horsepower gives this car quite the punch despite the car being in a D Class license series.

Newest GT3 racer to come to iRacing as of September 2023, the Ferrari 296 GT3 is the newest of Ferrari's GT3 racing machines ready to tear up the track on raceday. The car comes with many features, components and more, one of them being its engine, a Ferrari F163CE V6 GDI Turbo packing 600 horsepower. Other features include a Transversal sequential gearbox with an 6 speed e-clutch actuator transmission and a double wishbone, tubular steel suspension arm with aluminum uprights and even adjustable dampers. This gives the car ample suspension, durability, toughness, and a smooth transition for shifting through the gears. The last feature on this car to point out is that it also has brake calipers with the fronts having 6 pistons and the rear having 4 pistons helping the car to slow down or stop whenever its needed. No matter what though, this Ferrari 296 GT3 is ready to race.

An improvement in GT3 racing, the Ferrari 488 is a racer that brings shame to others and glory for itself. Coming from Italy and with over 400 horsepower, this car drives like a dream. Based on the road going Ferrari 488 car, the GT3 version comes with a 6-speed dual clutch with carbon-ceramic brakes to increase stopping distances to a bare minimum. With disc sizes 9% smaller than the previous 458, this car stops quicker and brakes harder like no other. With under body vortex generators to reduce air pressure, this car is a true scientific achievement in the racing world.

Gleaming on to the track in fresh, bright Rosso Corsa paint, the new Ferrari 488 GT3 EVO is probably one of the most sophisticated and technologically advanced GT3 cars on the road racing circuit. The 600 horses that are delivered to this beast comes from a 3.9 liter twin-turbo V8 VVT powered engine that knows how to lay the power down with its mid-engine RWD layout for any balanced feel for any driver. A weight of 1260 kg keeps the car light enough to speed off the line but its not too heavy to bog it down. The grip from its Pirelli F-Zero racing tires makes it unparalleled among many other cars in its class and gives the car very good traction on any racetrack. The vehicle finally features a Fabricated steel-double wishbone with multi-links to give it added handling to an already powerful vehicle.

A thoroughbred, the 488 GTE is Ferrari’s latest Sports Car and GT Car racer it has to offer. Its engine spitting over 450 hp brings drivers a whole new flavor to the road course racing world. A more tuned up version of its GT3 counterpart, the GTE version (GTLM for North America) brings in scalloped side air intakes and increased radiator cooling. The car itself has 50% more downforce than the 458 while reducing aerodynamic drag at the same time. With a new Aero Pillar that deflects air under the car's flat body makes this car one of the most advanced racecars in the world of motorsport.

The newest LMDh / GTP to hit the iRacing scene of an ever-growing list of prototype race cars, Ferrari's 499P LMDh / GTP seems to be quite the answer in providing iRacers with a 5th option in the LMDh / GTP field competing alongside Acura, BMW, Cadillac, and Porsche. The car features a Ferrari F163 Twin-Turbo V6 Hybrid with a Front-Mounted 200KW spec MGU electric motor giving it the power it needs to power through corners and speed down straightaways. Other features of the car include a carbon composite monocoque chassis, a double wishbone with pushrod activation suspension, a 6 piston caliper carbon rotor braking system and with Michelin tires and a 7 speed sequential paddle shift transmission makes this Ferrari a very technologically advanced car.

Tatuus' F4-T021 has entered the sim in the presence with help from iRacing.com Motorsport Simulations also known as the Formula iR-04. With a 2.0L inline-4 cylinder engine making 160 hp, the car may not be very powerful but with its weight of 1257 lbs, it can comfortably get up to 150 mph. Other features on the car include a dry sump lubrication, water and air cooler cooling system, 6 speed sequential paddle shift gearbox, front and rear double wishbone suspension, and 2 piston Brembo brake calipers. All of this technology and with adjustable front and rear wings, this car is definitely sure to be a fan favorite on iRacing.

A new lead design for GT3 racing, the GT GT3 from Ford gives over 550 horsepower like no other. 30 gallons of fuel makes it a true racer in 24 hour racing. Basically a downgraded version from its Ford GT counterpart, it is still a fast GT3 car for asphalt road races alike. While still using the same 6 speed transmission as the Ford GT, the car remains a formidable racing car to many alike. Not as flashy and fancy as the new Ford GT GTE, no matter what though, this GT3 variant is still alive and kicking.

Ready to take on the Ferrari 488 GTE and other GTE cars alike, the new Ford GT GTE remains a popular road course figure as it won the Le Mans LM GTE Pro Class in June of 2016. Its power and speed are no laughing matter when driving this eccentric racecar. With Ford announcing the new Ford GT GTE for the 2016 24 Hours of Le Mans, it was Ford Chip Ganassi Racing that campaigned in that years IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship and also the FIA World Endurance Championship. When the 2017 24 Hours of Le Mans was over, the #67 car finished runner up at that year's 24 Hours of Le Mans in the GTE Pro Class while in the previous year it finished 7th and 9th. The car has been improved since then and is now ready for any 24 Hours of Le Mans race.

A 330 horsepower Mustang FR500S gives road racing a whole new meaning to Ford. Its top speed of 158 mph makes it easy to control. Based on the Mustang FR500 road going variant, the S model of the Mustang FR500 was designed by Ford Racing and Miller Motorsports for the Ford Racing Mustang Challenge series. It features aerodynamic parts like any other Mustang but with DOT approved racing BF Goodrich g-Force R1 tires for good grip, good handling, and improved stability. Now homologated for the SCCA World Challenge GTS Class, this car has been a great tool in the Ford Racing lineup where ever it goes to.

engine: Ford Coyote 5.4 Liter Naturally Aspirated V8
bio: The newest generation of Ford's road racing fleet, the Mustang GT3 powered by its Coyote 5.4 Liter Naturally Aspirated V8 built by Multimatic for IMSA and FIA racing alike, this car is ready for many seasons worth of competition at any road course. This vehicle itself marks the first time since 1997 that a Mustang will compete at the Circuit des 24 Heures du Mans, a 27 year gap. With past Le Mans drivers now a part of the Ford factory IMSA program, this car seems to be quite a winner indeed. The car features double wishbone with Multimatic DSSV dampers for its suspension, Alcon brakes, a carbon propshaft, a four plate Ap racing clutch, and a Xtrac Six Speed transaxle with ESA shift transmission giving this car a lot of technological innovation to show off to many racing fans around the globe to both the casual and the hardcore.

The newest GT4 in iRacing and also the first American GT4 in the sim, the Ford Mustang GT4 is the 6th GT4 to come to iRacing and is definitely full of features. The engine is a 5.0L Coyote V8 Naturally Aspirated giving it a loud and proud 500 horsepower. The car also comes with a 6 speed sequential transmission and its chassis is a unibody with natural fiber composites. Other features of this car include a MacPherson strut front, multi-link rear suspension and Brembo brakes with 6-piston action on the front and 4-piston action on the rear with iron rotors and ABS giving it ample braking power and Michelin tires giving the car grip to plow through its competition on raceday.

To start off a young driver’s F1 career, the Formula Renault 2.0 is the way to go. It’s power, speed, and aerodynamics give the car grip like no other F1 starter car. With a torsion bar, push-rod, twin strut suspension, this car gets around the corners with plenty of ease and with very little difficulty. The tires themselves are both Michelin branded and are a good racing treat to use come rain or shine. With the wheels having a single piece magnesium, this car and its agility makes it one of the most prominent open wheeler cars that any asphalt road race driver can use. __NOEDITSECTION__

The new Formula Vee from Sheane's Formula Vee - Classic is definitely one of the most fun and interesting cars to drive. While it only has a piffling 85 horsepower, this car can still reach 100 mph. It has a Volkswagen type 3 1200cc engine with external oil coolers and oil filters for max cooling. The car also has a 4 speed h-shifter transmission with hydraulic linkage for its clutch. The brakes are also hydraulic with disc brakes in the front and drum brakes in the back. The steering is rack and pinion giving the car good handling on any short road course. This vehicle will definitely be one of the popular vehicles in iRacing as it is now the 2nd option for a rookie to begin their road racing career.

The new Formula Vee - Conqueror is one of two new Formula Vee cars to come to iRacing to complement the Sheane Formula Vee - Classic. The features between it and the others are pretty much identical except the body shape. Regardless, the car is powered by a Volkswagen Type 3 (1200 cc) engine that is air cooled with external oil coolers and oil filters, a stock Volkswagen transmission that is 4 speed, coil and distributor ignition, a stock Volkswagen with hydraulic linkage Clutch, hydraulic brakes with discs on the front and drums on the back, and the usual rack and pinion steering column giving this formula vee car a worthy competitor to the 2 other formula vee's come any raceday, rain or shine.

wiki_title: Sabre Racing Cars Formula Vee - Cutlass
bio: The new Formula Vee - Cutlass from Sabre Racing Cars is one of two new Formula Vee additions to iRacing to complement the Sheane Formula Vee - Classic car. The engine is the same Volkswagen Type 3 (1200cc) air cooled engine but still features a coil and distributor ignition, a stock Volkswagen with hydraulic linkage clutch, hydraulic with disc front brakes and rear drum brakes, and a rack and pinion steering column making the cutlass model of the formula vee a well-improved model with some very nice refinements.

The Gen 4 Grand National car borrows aspects of the Impala SS that NASCAR's Nationwide Series used in 2009 with it being reflected in iRacing as a whole. Besides that the car is powered by a 650 horsepower 358 Cubic Inch Pushrod V8 giving it the beefy power that it desires. Other features of the car include a steel tube frame, a 4 speed transmission, and A-arm front with truck arm rear suspension designed for use with coil-bind spring setups with sway bars and spring rates with adjustable ride heights and track bar heights giving the car any oval suspension flexibility for any raceday. The car's fuel tank in real life can be filled with unleaded or leaded gasoline (petrol), and has a 12:1 carburetor compression ratio with a naturally aspirated size of 390 cubic foot per minute. This makes this car a true beast on any oval racetrack.

wiki_type: Beginner GT and Beginner Prototype Racer
bio: A beginner’s road course car, the Global MX-5 Cup has a balanced feel and a great way to start a road course career in a sim or in the real world. With the car being based on its road going Mazda MX-5 counterpart, its one of the greatest rookie asphalt road racers of its current time. With its invitational series today having 19 drivers from 8 different countries, this Mazda is a global star in its own right. Having its own series sanctioned from SCCA Pro racing to INDYCAR, the promotions are now controlled by Andersen Promotions that controls and runs promotions and sanctioning of many series for all to enjoy.

A new addition to the TCR circuit, the Honda Civic Type R with its V-TEC power is definitely one of the newest innovations taking the series by storm. The car itself with a weight over 2700 lbs make it quite the heavy hitter out there to anyone that oppose it. Other features of the car include McPherson strut coil springs and gas-filled dampers for thefront suspension and a multi-link axle with coil springs for the rear suspension along with the gas-filled dampers. Both front and rear suspension include the standard anti-roll bar and all of this leads to a car with a good acceleration time and a marginally good top speed giving the car plenty of power and grip.

engine: LM-V8, ACO IMSA LMP2Power: 486.66 hp (480 bhp) (357.94 kw)
bio: With its LM-V8 engine, this LMP2 ARX-01c tames Le Mans like no other LMP2 car on the circuit even to this date. Honda is well known for F1 and Le Mans racing. Previously known as the Acura ARX-01c before its change to the Honda HPD ARX-01c, the car features a double wishbone, coil spring suspension with anti-roll bars and dampers to provide maximum racing comfort. Its carbon fibre and aluminum monocoque chassis keeps the cars' weight to an absolute minimum. Using Castrol EDGE as its lubricant and Michelin and Dunlop as its main tires, the ARX-01c car is a LMP2 car that has long gone by.

Hyundai's newest racecar for the touring car circuit, the Elantra CN7, is ready for the track to go up against Honda's Civic Type R and Audi's RS3 LMS. The car itself is loaded with tons of innovations and technological enhancements over quite a varied amount of areas. The car's transmission and gearbox is a 6 speed sequential with paddle shift and acerametallic twin-disc clutch with a multi-plate limited slip differential for ease of gear shifting. Other features include a McPherson strut with coil springs and gas-filled dampers with anti-roll bars on the front suspension with the 4-arm multi-link axle on the rear suspension. Other areas include electric powered steering and dual circuit hydraulic brakes for max handling and braking power. While the front brakes are six-piston calipers at 380mm, the rear brakes are two-piston calipers at 278mm. The fuel system is a 100 liter (26.42 gallon) fuel tank for long endurance racing and lastly with a OMP race seat with 6 point HANS compatiable harness with info pages for its interior. The car itself is ready to race for anyone that drives it.

Hyundai's 2nd vehicle in iRacing, the Veloster N TCR is definitely quite the beast. Also being the fastest TCR car to date, this car does boast the similar power, weight, engine, and same drive configuration as the other TCR cars but has its own party treats. The car itself has a 6 speed sequential paddle shift with cerametallic twin-disc clutch and a multi-plate limited slip differential with strut coil springs and gas filled chambers for delivering power and giving it good handling. It also has electrical power assisted rack and pinion steering for precision movement and modern brakes, brake calipers, fuel system, standard racing interior, and others. This car itself is ready to race.

Italian power in this small but nimble USF Pro 2000 PM18 for the Indy Lights series makes this car fun but also competitive. Using the Mazda 2.0 Liter for power, this car is ready for racing. The car features a Mazda 2 Liter MZR-PM18A engine which gives it 275 horsepower, this car and its 10.6 gallon fuel tank and 1102 lbs of weight is a true lightweight car that's definitely got a kick to its acceleration. Being only a little faster than the old Pro Mazda, this car also features more technological features that the older car didn't have.

A Korean feat of engineering, the Optima GX deploys over 350 horsepower to the road like no other. Its speed of over 170 mph is in a class of its own in a racing world that races over 200 mph today. Based upon its road going Kia Optima counterpart, this very same vehicle is part of the 4th Generation of the Kia Optima known as the Kia Optima JF and related to the Hyundai Sonata LF model. Being the front wheel drive powered car in the iRacing field, this vehicle is surely in a class of its own.

The Lamborghini Huracán GT3 EVO is the newest GT3 car to hit the iRacing scene and has definitely a lot of potential to be a great car for the road racing GT3 community. With 500 horsepower coming from its 5.2 liter naturally aspirated V10 engine, this car is no slouch in delivering its power to the road and it has a really good acceleration time too. With a midweight of just under 3000 lbs and a fuel capacity of exactly 120 liters, this car can go long distances before needing another top-up of fuel. With a name and car like Lamborghini, its definitely gonna square off against the Ferrari 488 GT3 for dominance between the two well-known Italian car makes. While one of these cars will win the battle, it all comes down to which car will win the war.

Newest late model stock vehicle that has replaced the old Chevy Monte Carlo SS, the CARS Late Model Stock is a 500 hp V8 roaring beast for many short tracks and mile oval tracks throughout the southeast. The car has double arm suspension with coil over shocks and springs combined with a truck arm and track bar giving it the stability, agility, and proper turn-in needed to get around the tight short tracks and wider mile oval tracks with relative ease. The car also features a 4 speed manual transmission with 475 foot pounds of torque giving it some serious muscle out on the track.

One of iRacing’s oldest cars, the Ford ‘34 Coupe can deliver fun and excitement to Rookies and Pros alike. Its Yamaha engine powers the car quickly to compensate for its 1100 lb. weight. The car is based on '34 models of its heyday and it uses 595 Federal Tires for racedays on its schedule. With the weight being under 1 US Ton (2000 lbs, 907 kg), this tiny car remains a popular short-track racing vehicle to many people that go to those tracks. Not a very fast racecar but to the fans, action and good fun matters the most.

The 4th french car to the service and the 2nd french manufacturer to appear in iRacing, the Ligier JS P320 LMP3 is iRacing's first LMP3 racer. As any other racecar, this new LMP3 features many modern features that are standard and equipped on today's racecars. Besides its 450+ horsepower Nissan VK56 5.6 Liter V8 engine, the car is equipped with a variety of technologically advanced base features. Such features like Monocoque carbon chassis for lightweightness and durability, Double wishbone and Pushrod and spring-damper combination, Adjustable anti-roll bar system, 6-speed sequential gearbox Xtrac 1152 with aluminium casing, and even Hydraulic power-assisted steering cooled by the cars oil radiator makes this vehicle a very well-made product for a wide variety of road racing circuits that await for its visit.

With its DOHC V8 405 hp engine, the Lotus 49 represents a true icon of classic Formula One racing. Classic drivers like Jim Clark and Graham Hill graced the car with pristine glory and pride forever. The car features an aluminum monocoque chassis while using Firestone or Dunlop tires to keep this cars' weight down and to provide a smoother ride. Being most famously shown in its Gold and British Racing Green colors, the Lotus 49 started off as a troubled car for a few years but became one of the most fantastic Formula 1 cars of its time. With top speeds over 200 mph, drivers fought this car to stay alive.

The Famous Lotus 79 constructed for the 1978 Formula One season is still titled as one of Formula One’s greatest cars. With it’s 32 valve DOHC Cosworth DFV V8 engine, its one heck of a beast. Being the first Formula 1 car to take maximum advantage of aerodynamics and startling ground effects, this car uses the same Aluminum Monocoque chassis as its previous Lotus 49 from the 60's. The car also uses a double wishbone suspension with inboard springs and dampers for the front and parallel top links, lower wishbone, twin radius arms for its rear suspension. Goodyear tires keep the cars' grip to a max sticking to the track come rain or shine. With famous drivers like Mario Andretti winning the 1978 Drivers Championship and Constructors Championship, this impressive car shows others what they were missing out on ever since debuting in its first race at the 1978 Belgian Grand Prix at Circuit Zolder.

The newest GT4 car to hit the iRacing scene and a long awaited arrival, the Mclaren 570S GT4 has many things for it. The car is powered by a 3.8 Liter twin Turbo V8 M838TE engine that makes over 450 horsepower giving this car the acceleration and speed that it desires. The vehicle has a 7 speed SSG transmission for easy shifting through the gears and rides on a McLaren carbon fibre MonoCell II chassis with aluminium front and rear frames and crash structures for outstanding durability. Also the car has a body of aluminium and carbon panels to keep it lightweight and aerodynamics of both front splitter and rear spoiler for racecar handling on any road course. The car uses Pirelli racing 265/645 and 305/680 tires and a 110 liter fuel cell for endurance and long racing stints. For a car that seems to do plenty, this vehicle is definitely gonna be a favorite and will lead to many battles between the BMW and Porsche rivals.

New and innovative, the McLaren 720S GT3 Evo is ready to hit the road racing scene all across the world. With over 700 horsepower coming from its M840T 4.0 liter Twin-Turbocharged V8 engine, this gives the car an insane 0-60 time of just 2.8 seconds, faster than any other GT3 car out on the circuit today. With a mid-engine RWD layout, drivers will have to keep the car balanced as much as possible or risk spinning out. This machine also features a six-speed sequential transmission, adjustable dampers with coil-over springs, a carbon fiber MonoCage II chassis, FIA safety with rollcages, side-impact, foam, and a roof hatch extraction system giving the car the technology it demands. Other features of the car also include a lightweight carbon fiber composite body with a front splitter and floor assembly, dive planes, motorsport axles with single wheel retaining nuts, and the standard winged-headrest seat with six-point harness making the car a true technological masterpiece.

With its V8 engine, the MP4-12C GT3 is a monster in GT racing. With a top speed of over 170 mph, it’s a powerful brute on the circuit. Based on the road going McLaren MP4-12C (later became the McLaren 12C respectively), this car is also related to the McLaren P1 and the McLaren 650S models as well. The body of the car uses carbon fibre to bring weight down to an absolute minimum and to provide better acceleration. The chassis known as the Carbon MonoCell is a very light weight system that makes the car very nimble on both straightaways and the turns. Having top speeds very close to the Porsche 911 GT3 Cup (991) and the Mercedes AMG GT3 vehicles, this car brings out the best in racers and simracers that drive this highly strung vehicle.

engine: V8 Front Mid-Engine; DOHC 4 valves per cylinder
bio: Sinister but yet tame, the Mercedes-Benz AMG GT3 is the collaboration of Mercedes-Benz and AMG to make the road-going SLS a car to keep tabs on during race day. The characteristics of the car features lightweight body and chassis to keep weight down and acceleration up. Being a predecessor to the Mercedes-Benz 300SL and the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren, it is truly a monster on the track. Despite the Mercedes-Benz AMG GT being its successor, this car makes other race car drivers envy of the way it performs, drives, and how it handles.

Featuring new technology and a new mightier engine, the 2020 version of Merc's AMG GT3 has come to iRacing finally at last. With 550 horsepower from its AMG 6.3 Liter V8 Naturally Aspirated engine, the car has enough power for any GT3 driver. The vehicle has many other features as well including a Sequential AMG 6-gear racing transmission, motorsports electronics, multiple-adjustable ABS, AMG Traction Control, and many others. The wheels are AMG Alloys and the chassis is a double wishbone with configurable rebound and pressure dampers with configurable stabilizers. With a 28 gallon fuel endurance length tank, the car and its weight of just under 3000 lbs make the car quite the beast out on the track.

engine: AMG 4.0 Liter V8 BiturboPower: 544 hp (536.56 bhp) (400.111 kw)
bio: A newest GT4 to hit the iRacing GT4 scene, the Mercedes-Benz AMG GT4 is the newest entry for GT4 cars in iRacing. With a AMG 4.0 liter V8 biturbo engine, this makes the car output quite a whopping 544 horsepower. The vehicle is also equipped with a sequential AMG 6-gear racing transmission with motorsports electronics, multiple-adjustable ABS, and even AMG traction control making this car advanced in its technology. Other features of the car include a double wishbone chassis with configurable rebound and pressure dampers that feature configurable stabilizers. With a weight of just over 3000 pounds, the car can throw its weight around and survive making this vehicle quite a tank in its own right.

wiki_title: Mercedes-Benz AMG F1 W12 E Performance
engine: Mercedes-Benz AMG F1 M12 E Performance 1.6 Liter V6
bio: The newest F1 car to come to iRacing after a long 6 years has finally arrived with the Mercedes-Benz AMG F1 W12 E Performance. This car itself having over 1,000 horsepower from its V6 engine delivers the power fast and hard to ensure its dominant place in the field. The car itself is chocked full of innovations, technology, and other cool tricks to make it stand out from other F1 cars. The moulded carbon fibre and honeycomb composite structure monocoque design ensure complete safety of the driver in the event of a crash. The bodywork is also carbon fibre composite and the cockpit features a removable drivers seat made of anatomically formed carbon composite with the OMP six-point driver safety harness and HANS system. Other safety structures include a cockpit survival cell incorporating impact-resistant construction and penetration panels with front impact structure, prescribed side impact structures, integrated rear impact structure, front and rear roll structures, and titanium driver protection structure to meet its highly safety standard requirements. The suspension on the car is carbon fibre wishbone and pushrod-activated for smooth rides over bumpy surfaces on any F1 track it goes to. The Carbone Industries carbon discs with Brembo brake calipers are the brakes that slow or stop this powerful beast of a car. FIA standard ECU and FIA homologated electronic and electrical system rely all the information to the driver that it can possibly deliver along with its McLaren Electronic System. The ATL Kevlar-reinforced rubber bladder fuel system makes its fuel tank safe in any serious crash. Finally the carbon plate clutch with the sequential semi auto-matic eight speed gearbox give the car both the acceleration and top speed it deserves. This makes this car a true beast out on the track.

wiki_title: Mercedes-Benz AMG F1 W13 E Performance
engine: Mercedes-AMG F1 M13 E Performance 1.6 liter direct injection turbocharged V6
bio: Mercedes-Benz' newest F1 car for iRacing the AMG F1 W13 E Performance is loaded with technology and performance for 2022. The car features a Mercedes-AMG F1 M13 E Performance 1.6 liter direct injection turbocharged V6engine with a Motor Generator Unit Kinetic electric motor for over 1,000 horsepower. The car itself is a molded carbon fibre monocoque shell for light weight and strong durability with a carbon fibre bodywork for extra strength. The suspension are carbon fibre wishbone and pushroad-activated torsion springs for strong relative motion and even carbone industries carbon discs for its brakes gives the car ample braking power. With power-assissted steering, ECU electronics, MES instrumentation, ATL Kevlar-reinforced fuel system and a 8 speed sequential semi automatic hydraulic activated gearbox, this car is ready for raceday.

Featuring the same technical specifications as its dirt oval counterpart, the mini stock is a fine small asphalt oval racecar for short oval and mile oval use and does it really well in local races across the country. With a 2.3 Liter Inline 4 Cylinder 2V OHC engine making 200 horsepower, OEM strut 4-link coil springs for its suspension, OEM disk and drum brakes, along with Hoosier racing tires and a Modified OEM frame with reinforced roll cage, the car is a near 1-to-1 exact of its dirt counterpart with the main difference is its main use for asphalt short track and mile oval racing. Nevertheless the similarities, the mini stock and its dirt counterpart are bound to be fan favorites. One thing to note is that the dirt mini stock counterpart revs up to 8,500 rpm's while the regular asphalt mini stock only revs up to 7,500 rpm's.

370 horsepower and open wheel racing, the SK Modified is one fast gerbil of a car. A top speed of over 140 mph makes it a quick bullet out on the racing circuit. Being a less powerful version of its Whelen Modified Tour counterpart, the SK Modified remains a quick and fast car. Even though it has 250 less hp and 15 less mph top speed than the Whelen Modified Tour counterpart, the car is still worth its weight and might around the track. Drivers are often started in the SK Modified before moving up to the Whelen Modified Tour car due to the fact that the Whelen Modified Tour car boasts over 600 horsepower and top speeds almost nearing 160 mph.

wiki_title: NASCAR Cup Series Chevrolet Camaro ZL1
bio: A new Gen 6 monster to devour the competition, Chevrolet brings out all the stops with their new Camaro ZL1 to take the fight to Ford and Toyota. With the car weighing 100 lbs less than its Chevy SS predecessor, this gives the car a 0-60 mph (0-100 kmh) acceleration improvement of 0.2 seconds from 2.9 to 2.7 seconds. The vehicle's chassis is the Mild-Steel with Full Rollcage for maximum car and driver protection. With 750 horsepower compared to its Chevy SS predecessor of over 850 hp, this means the car itself is a bit nerfed when it comes to power, acceleration and speed at the Superspeedways. With a 4 speed manual transmission for optimal gear selection and efficiency, a steel and carbon bodywork for maximum durability, and a SLA Front, truck arm rear suspension, this new thoroughbred is ready for any competition it meets out on the track.

The new Monster Energy Ford car to take to the NASCAR circuit, this Mustang is ready to take on any car that comes its way. The past Fusion has been replaced by this new thoroughbred of a racecar that lays power down like no other NASCAR cup series racing machine. Featuring new aerodynamic and downforce technology the new Monster Energy Cup Ford Mustang remains one of the more exquisite NASCAR vehicles on the circuit today. Not all the much different from its previous Ford Fusion model, this one should feel quite similar to drive.

wiki_title: NASCAR Cup Series Next Gen Chevrolet Camaro ZL1
bio: The newest NASCAR next gen (or gen 7) cup cars have finally been launched to iRacing and they are definitely quite a different breed compared to the previous gen 6. One of the biggest changes is from the h-shifter 4 gear pattern to the sequential 5 gear pattern to make shifting up and down through the gears easier for the driver. The car features newly designed aero and downforce package and a redesigned side skirt which reduce the side force in the vehicle. Also included is a rear diffuser for the first time in a NASCAR cup series car. Some of the newest technological improvements on the car include a spec chassis, independent rear suspension, new wheel design, and a new refueling system similar to those used in the IMSA Series. The weight of the car is a bit heavier than its gen 6 predecessors but these cars are ready for the cup tracks of today and also yesteryear too.

wiki_title: NASCAR Cup Series Next Gen Ford Mustang
bio: The newest NASCAR next gen (or gen 7) cup cars have finally been launched to iRacing and they are definitely quite a different breed compared to the previous gen 6. One of the biggest changes is from the h-shifter 4 gear pattern to the sequential 5 gear pattern to make shifting up and down through the gears easier for the driver. The car features newly designed aero and downforce package and a redesigned side skirt which reduce the side force in the vehicle. Also included is a rear diffuser for the first time in a NASCAR cup series car. Some of the newest technological improvements on the car include a spec chassis, independent rear suspension, new wheel design, and a new refueling system similar to those used in the IMSA Series. The weight of the car is a bit heavier than its gen 6 predecessors but these cars are ready for the cup tracks of today and also yesteryear too.

wiki_title: NASCAR Cup Series Next Gen Toyota Camry
engine: 358 Cubic Inch 5.8 Liter EFI V8Power: 670 hp (660.8 bhp) (492.8 kw)
bio: The newest NASCAR next gen (or gen 7) cup cars have finally been launched to iRacing and they are definitely quite a different breed compared to the previous gen 6. One of the biggest changes is from the h-shifter 4 gear pattern to the sequential 5 gear pattern to make shifting up and down through the gears easier for the driver. The car features newly designed aero and downforce package and a redesigned side skirt which reduce the side force in the vehicle. Also included is a rear diffuser for the first time in a NASCAR cup series car. Some of the newest technological improvements on the car include a spec chassis, independent rear suspension, new wheel design, and a new refueling system similar to those used in the IMSA Series. The weight of the car is a bit heavier than its gen 6 predecessors but these cars are ready for the cup tracks of today and also yesteryear too.

Power and grip for NASCAR vehicles are presented in the latest rendition of NASCAR’s Toyota Camry. Over 800 horsepower and speeds in excess of 190 mph gives this NASCAR speed a new nickname in the sport. Toyota has been with NASCAR ever since debuting in 2004 for the Camping World Series and 2007 for the Xfinity and Monster Energy series. Still using the same 5.9 liter pushrod V8 as the other NASCAR vehicles, the weight of 3300 lbs and the 2.9 0-60 mph acceleration time make it a fan favorite and a driver favorite for all to enjoy come qualifying, practice, and also racedays. When the might of this car comes around the track though, drivers still feel its presence and are aware of what they see in front or what they feel is coming behind them.

A classic NASCAR cup racer that brings a lot of nostalgia with it, the NASCAR Chevrolet Monte Carlo Gen 4 Cup car is definitely a vehicle that harkens back to NASCAR's golden era. The Gen 4 cars themselves lasting from 1992 to 2006 still have an everlasting impact on many racing fans young and old. The car has all of the NASCAR typical features like the classic 4 speed manual transmission, a 22 gallon fuel tank, standard NASCAR weight of 3400 lbs, a steel tube frame chassis and roll cage, and a double A-arm front and truck arm with panhard bar rear for its suspension gives the car that nostalgic 2003 feel.

The main rival to the NASCAR Chevrolet Monte Carlo Gen 4, the NASCAR Ford Taurus Gen 4 is a worthy opponent as the two makes have battled each other through thick and thin ever since the beginning of NASCAR's days in 1949. With an intense rivalry lasting well over half a century by 2003 and three-quarters of a century by 2024, these two titans are still serious fighters today. Like the NASCAR Chevrolet Monte Carlo Gen 4, the features of this car are very similar featuring the same 900 horsepower with its 90 degree pushrod V8 358 Cubic Inch engine, 4 speed manual transmission, a 22 gallon fuel tank, the standard NASCAR Cup 3400 lbs weight, a steel tube frame chassis, and a double A-arm front and truck arm with panhard bar rear suspension although besides the many similarities, the Ford Taurus itself is a beast in its own right.

The speediness of the Buick LeSabre has finally come to iRacing and it shows. With a car that shares many of the same characteristics as the other Gen 3 1987 vehicles in the sim, the car features a Borg Warner Super T-10 4 speed manual and independent front suspension with coil springs and anti-rollbar giving the car acceleration and handling. With a live axle truck arm and with power coming from its 358 cubic inch V8 engine, the car is ready to battle it out on the track once more against Chevrolet and Ford. Just remember that like the Chevrolet Monte Carlo and Ford Thunderbird, this car comes with no power steering.

A blast from the NASCAR racing past, this Gen 3 Monte Carlo from the 1987 season makes its entry into iRacing. While it may not be up to spec with today’s racecars, this car brings memories back for many people. With a powerful 358 Cubic Inch Chevy V8 blasting out 650 horsepower through its blow overs and a hefty weight of 3700 lbs, this car is also a handful to drive. This vehicle and its counterpart, the Ford Thunderbird, do not feature any power steering whatsoever so a pair of muscles might be necessary to wheel this beast around any oval racetrack.

Another classic Gen 3 NASCAR from the 1987 season, the Thunderbird makes its entry into iRacing to compete with the 1987 Monte Carlo. Full of its own memories, this car is ready to whiz around any racetrack. This car and its 351 Cubic Inch Ford V8 weighing at 3700 lbs is ready for stiff and heavy competition against the Gen 3 NASCAR Chevrolet Monte Carlo on any track during any weekend of the year. While it may has less horsepower than its Chevy counterpart, it has a slightly higher power to weight ratio which gives it just a little more kick in its acceleration. The true test for sure is if anybody on iRacing can beat the 212.809 mph qualifying speed set by Bill Elliot at Talladega in 1987 with a lap time of 44.998 seconds.

The new Pontiac Grand Prix - 1987 Gen 3 car is the 4th addition to iRacing's NASCAR gen 3 class cars from the 1987 season. The car while has similarities to the others like same fuel capacity, same weight, and similar acceleration time and configuration, this car still has some differences besides the badge on the car. For starters, the car has a Borg Warner super T-10 4-speed manual transmission, and the independent with coil springs and anti-rollbar with live axle truck arm suspension gives the car the typical gen 3 1987 technology and features that makes the Pontiac Grand Prix a blast from the past.

The new Camaro for the NASCAR’s XFINITY series, this new rendition of the car makes the competition all the more tougher and the action more spectacular. The new aerodynamic possibilities from the new Chevrolet Camaro means the car is a bit more fuel-efficient than its previous generations. This reduces drag slightly while also making more downforce on the car making it more stable. Inside the car, the interior is all but different for each model. On the Camaro, the gauges are in the center and also to the left. The car also itself features a strong metal body to keep its drivers safe from any nasty wrecks that happen during raceday.

Ford has brought out the new Mustang rendition to battle against the new Camaro and the new Supra. Time will tell if this will work to Ford’s advantage or not. The car follows the guidelines of the other XFINITY cars in its field with a 358 Cubic Inch V8 engine, 650 horsepower, and the standard 18.5 gallon fuel tank. With weight now under 3500 lbs, the car is a tad lighter giving slightly more acceleration. The vehicle's gauges itself are all on the center row to give maximum visibility to the driver no matter where the steering wheel input is. With top speeds over 180 mph and a very good 0-60 acceleration time, this new Mustang seems ready for the oval racing scene.

The new Supra is one of the oddest looking NASCAR vehicles but one day may prove its dominance on the track. Same 358 Cubic Inch V8 engine with 650 hp as its other XFINITY counterparts, the XFINITY Toyota Supra may be one of the more interesting NASCAR shapes to enter into the modern era of NASCAR racing. With same 18.5 gallon fuel tank and 3450 lb weight as other XFINITY current gen vehicles, this Supra is ready to race alongside its fellow competitors. Like the Mustang, the gauges are in the center though it has one extra gauge to the right hand side. The oddball bit about the Supra's interior is that for gauge count, the Camaro and Mustang have 7 gauges while the Supra has 6 gauges making this car a truly unique racing machine.

The new Silverado for the Craftsman Truck Series is truly a new advancement in technology. The downforce and aerodynamics of this vehicle is better than previous truck generations. Part of the new generation of NASCAR Truck series vehicles, this all-new model featuring new cutting edge technology both on the interior and exterior keeps the driver safe from any hard-hitting accident out on the track. The power, engine, fuel, and weight are the same from the previous incarnation of the truck series which makes this truck all the more easier to drive for even the inexperienced of drivers.

The 3rd brand of the NASCAR Craftsman Trucks has made its way into iRacing in the form of the F150. This new throroughbred is full of power, prestige, and excitement to keep fans glued to their seats. Finally adding the final truck that is part of NASCAR's Craftsman truck series, this modern truck racer can now finally race in iRacing competitions alongside its Chevrolet Silverado and Toyota Tundra enemies. Using the same engine, weight, and almost similar top speed as the others, this truck can be competitive if a driver knows how to wheel one of these powerful beasts that need a whole lot of taming.

The new Ram 1500 for NASCAR's Craftsman truck series seems to be a call back to the days when Dodge used to be in the truck series until for a while it went down to 3 manufacturers between Chevrolet, Ford, and Toyota. For the Craftsman Truck Series, the 4 brand battle is now back with a new face but carries some familiar roots and history. The new Ram 1500 is powered by a 650 horsepower Ilmor NT1 V8 engine with a 4 speed manual transmission built on a mild-steel and full roll cage chassis, an SLA front and truck arm live axle rear suspension with multipot caliper brakes on both front and rear axles and the good ole Goodyear Eagle tires gives this Ram 1500 some technological improves to brag about.

wiki_title: NASCAR Craftsman Toyota Tundra TRD Pro
bio: The Tundra’s OEM Cast-Iron Block engine produces over 600 horsepower. Even though the restrictor plate limits the car to under 200 mph, its still a high-powered racing vehicle on the track. Based on its road going Tundra variant, the Tundra truck is the other choice when choosing a vehicle to run in any truck series race. With weight over 3400 lbs and acceleration just at around the 4 second mark, no matter who drives this untamed beast, they are gonna have a great time driving it around the NASCAR racetracks no matter how easy or how difficult the challenge may be.

The new Whelen Modified is the true answer to modern open wheel oval racecars and this car is no exception. The power it lays down is truly amazing. The 600+ horsepower OEM Cast-Iron Block V8 engine produces an exquisite amount of torque making the car a quick accelerating beast. This ride itself needs whole new levels of taming even around the many short tracks that iRacing has today. With all new construction and many other technological advancements over the previous Whelen Modified model, the excitement that this new model will create will not go unnoticed by viewers, fans, and the drivers themselves.

Massive power and a 3,000 cc engine, the GTP ZX-T is one of the most fearsome cars on the racing circuit. With weight almost a ton, it has lightning fast acceleration of under 2 seconds. With its history starting back in 1984 when Nissan Motors started their long drive in the IMSA GT Championship, things first started off with the Lola T810 before gears shifted towards the GTP ZX-T with the T meaning "Turbo" thanks to its efficient turbocharger. Being the only car to crush the Porsche 962 by 11 seconds at Miami, this car showed its brute power and fast 0-60 2 second acceleration time makes other race cars truly fear it. With a narrow manufacturer championship defeat while winning the drivers championship in 1988, they came back in 1989 along with Geoff Brabham at the wheel crowning the Nissan GTP ZX-T in pure racing glory and triumph.

wiki_type: Beginner GT and Beginner Prototype Racer
bio: Made for road course beginners, the Pontiac Solstice teaches drivers the art of driving a road course car. With a small 2.0 Liter Ecotec engine producing only 177 horsepower, this car weighing only 2948 lbs makes it quite nippy on its feet when driving it around the track. With a 0-60 acceleration time of just under 8 seconds and a fuel capacity of just 14 gallons, not many people know the whereabouts of this car and since all new iRacers that sign up for the first time receive this car, it gives many drivers a great learning curve to those that deal with it.

wiki_type: Beginner GT and Beginner Prototype Racer
bio: The Rookie version of the Pontiac Solstice, this car teaches rookie drivers how to handle the real car. With the same 2.0 liter Ecotec and 177 horsepower engine as its non-rookie counterpart, the road-going Solstice is truly quite a beginners dream choice. With 0-60 acceleration time of just under 8 seconds and weight of just under 3000 lbs, it can still be an iRacer rookie car choice when given the proper tools and the proper learning to deal with the car. It teaches young iRacers how to handle road course vehicles on the asphalt and teaches them how to reach maximum grip and how to keep the car on the track.

One of Porsche’s newest racecars, the 718 Cayman GT4 Clubsport MR embodies everything that a Porsche should be. The speed, handling, and excitement that Porsche delivers is also shown in this very same racecar. The car features a 6 speed PDK dual-clutch automatic transmission for smooth transitions between upshifting and downshifting the gears. It also has ABS, traction control, and electronic stability control for ease of driving experience and skill to even the most novice of drivers. Also, the steering of the car is electrohydraulic power steering and also aluminum six piston brakes on the front and four piston brakes on the rear for maximum stopping and braking power. Finally, this Porsche features McPherson strut suspension on both front and rear for excellent rebounds over certain bumps on any racetrack that comes its way.

Featuring a bit more weight but more power than its predecessor, the 911 GT3 Cup (992.1), the new 911 GT3 Cup (992.2) is still full of its own surprises. The car has a Naturally Aspirated 4.0 Litre Flat-Six engine making 520 hp and a fuel tank capacity of 29 gallons (110 liters). The has a quick 0-60 time of just over 3 seconds and features a 6-speed sequential transmission, a unibody chassis with recycled composites, and a double wishbone multi-link suspension making it quite a capable machine. With Brembo piston brakes with iron rotors and ABS and Michelin wheels, it seems to be that this is the 911 GT3 Cup car of the future.

Porsche and its 4,000 cc DOHC flat-6 engine gives drivers thrill, but also fine mechanics that gives the 911 GT3 Cup (991) superiority in the field of motor racing across the whole world. Based on the famous Porsche 911 road going model, it features revised aerodynamics, improved rollcage, new wheels, and a revised chassis. The transmission inside the car is a paddle shift, race-bred, pneumatically-activated six speed that makes this car geared heavily towards trackdays and racedays alike. Using lightweight materials with a stripped-out cabin to keep weight as low as possible, it truly is a technological advancement in the racing world.

The newest GT3 Cup to hit the GT Cup racing scene brings out the 911 GT3 Cup (992.1) from Porsche. Their newest and latest high-tech thoroughbred is gonna become a hot contender on the road racing circuit and the features it has will definitely bring this car to a spotlight worthy of fame and fortune. The modern day technological advancements on the car include power assisted rack and pinion for precision steering, aluminum six piston brakes on the front tires and four piston brakes on the rear tires, and double wishbone suspension on the front tires with multi-link suspension on the rear tires. Finally, its 6 speed semi-automatic gearbox gives the car ease of upshifting and downshifting for efficient throttle control.

The Porsche 911 GT3 R is a cutting edge technically advanced vehicle from the giant automaker Porsche that is definitely a fan favorite to race today. It has a 520 horsepower water cooled 6-cylinder engine capable of delivering enough torque for the roaring beast. With a 31.7 gallon fuel tank and a weight of nearly 3000 lbs, this car can go the distance and throw itself around out on the racetrack. A 0-60 time of 2.8 seconds give it a fast acceleration and its mid-engine displacement keep the car balanced on the track. Other features of the car include Michelin 310/680-18 and 310/710-18 tires for very good gripping power, a 6-piston aluminum monobloc brake calipers for above average braking power, and a double wishbone and multilink suspension system with adjustable dampers and adjustable anti-roll bars for handling and stability. The car's transmission is a 6-speed constant-mesh sequential gearbox for smooth upshifts and downshifts and a direct fuel injection fuel feed with dry sump lubrication to keep it racing for hours on end making this car quite the vehicle to beat.

A new GT3 beast for the road racing scene the Porsche 911 GT3 R (992) is the replacement for the previous 911 GT3 R model from 2021. While its only been two years between the two cars, the improvements made on this vehicle over the last have definitely shown. Such improves for the car include a Single mass flywheel, Four-valve technology, Direct fuel injection, Dry sump lubrication with oil/water heat exchanger, Carbon fiber intake manifold, and many more coming from its water-cooled six-cylinder boxer engine making over 560 hp. The car also comes with many other improvements on its two axles such as independent rear suspension, High-performance spherical bearings, Wheel hubs with center lock wheel nuts, Motorsport dampers, Damper potentiometers, Shim adjustment system and high performance braking power from its brake discs and its brake calipers making this car very technologically advanced for the road racing scene at any road course circuit.

A breakthrough innovating in 911 Racing, the RSR GTE is the improved version of the GT3 Cup (991) and tuned to perfection by German Engineering. The cornering ability and the weight give the car a balanced feel throughout the entirety of the racing vehicle.
